saints.name: St. Elizabeth of Portugal
saints.title: Queen and Widow
saints.shortBlurb: A queen who bore the name of her great-aunt and gave her life to peacemaking and the poor…
biography: Named for her kinswoman St. Elizabeth of Hungary, she was born a princess of Aragon in 1271 and given in marriage to King Denis of Portugal. Amid a difficult marriage and a turbulent court she lived a life of prayer, penance, and generosity, founding hospitals, orphanages, and shelters and providing dowries for poor girls.

She is best remembered as a peacemaker, more than once riding onto the field between opposing armies — including those of her own husband and son — to reconcile them. After Denis died she became a Franciscan tertiary and lived near the Poor Clares at Coimbra, dying in 1336 while again on an errand of peace.
saints.knownFor: Making peace between warring kings and princes.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
